name: vol_breakout
description: Larry-Williams volatility breakout on 12 large-cap USDT perps (PIT top-20 liquidity mask). At each session open (UTC day, or 6h run) a server-side conditional stop-market entry at O +/- k*R with an attached stop at O -/+ s*R; time exit at the next session open. Trend filter: prior close vs MA(n days); optional BTC 200d-MA gate; shorts (L/S variant) only when coin < MA and BTC < 200d MA. Causal vol-target sizing (20%).
mechanism: Range expansion beyond the open is followed by same-session continuation (stop cascades, liquidations, late momentum entrants); the trend filter keeps moves aligned with the drift. Counterparty: range traders / short-gamma liquidity providers.

universe.tradable_mask: pit_top20 (Binance trailing-30d quote volume, re-ranked daily)
universe.column_choice: first 12 of data.MAJORS -- a fixed list of long-lived large caps, not chosen on performance but survivorship-biased (no LUNA/FTT-type collapses)

timeframe: 1h bars for intrabar trigger/stop resolution; orders placed at 1d (00 UTC) or 6h (00/06/12/18 UTC) session opens

harness.how_to_run: res = vol_breakout.simulate(panel, params)  # identical to: sp = vol_breakout.sim_panel(panel, params); entries, kw = vol_breakout.events(panel, params); sim.run_events(sp, entries, **kw)
harness.why: sim.run_events has NO conditional (stop) entry and no resting limit entry: every entry fills at the next bar OPEN. The module splits each 1h trigger bar into (open..trigger) and (trigger..close) rows so the entry fills AT the trigger and the attached stop is checked over the whole trigger hour (trigger + stop in the same hour = loss). Entries index the split panel via 't' (running them on the raw panel raises instead of mis-filling). wf.walk_forward cannot drive this directly (its sim panel = the strategy's input panel), so the walk-forward was re-implemented with wf.make_folds + the same train-only Sharpe selection + ONE stitched run_events OOS.

n_trials_note: 144 long-only configs (GRID). A separate 144-config L/S grid was also walk-forwarded (variant_long_short): 288 configs tried in total.

grid_summary.frozen_rule: max median Sharpe over the ten half-years 2020H2..2025H1 (tie-break: times chosen in WF)

wf.selection_note: each config simulated once over the dev period (strategy verified causal); train score = daily Sharpe inside the train window; the OOS is ONE stitched run_events simulation of the chosen configs' entries per test fold (capital carries over)

null.kind: random-day entries: each OOS trade keeps symbol/side/size/stop distance and fold window, entered at the open of a random session (same session length, symbol tradable) with the same stop and time exit; identical costs

implementability_200.note: same OOS entries as the headline, qty rounded down to Bybit qtyStep, orders below minOrderQty/minNotional dropped, $200 start

variant_long_short.note: same 144-config grid with shorts enabled (short only when coin prior close < MA(n) AND BTC < 200d MA); separate walk-forward; with the long-only grid 288 configs were tried in total

next_open_fill_variant_frozen_dev.note: FROZEN signals, but each entry fills at the open of the 1h bar AFTER the trigger bar (what run_events can express natively; needs hourly runs). Trigger-bar stop is skipped here, so this is NOT the pessimistic spec - shown only to size the modelling effect.

posthoc_diagnostics.note: POST-HOC diagnostics chosen after seeing the headline OOS (6h picked in fold 2023H2; BTC/ETH looked better in the in-sample comparison). Not the verdict basis; every extra grid adds trials (144 long + 144 L/S + 72 = 360).

live_targets_example.note: recompute trigger/stop from the ACTUAL session open price at the run

sizing.vol_estimate: trailing-180d realised vol of the unit (1%-risk) book from the rule's own CLOSED trades, BTC gate ignored; expanding window if < 20 active days; >= 60 days of history required
sizing.costs: taker 0.055%/side + lab slippage tiers (1bp BTC/ETH, 3bp majors, 8bp others) + 3bp extra on EVERY fill + actual Binance funding

run1_before_sizing_fix.why_changed: run 1 estimated vol from the GATED trade stream: after the 2022H2 fold (BTC gate on, zero trades) the estimate collapsed, the scale hit its 5x clip, and 2023H1 ran at 43% vol instead of 20%. Fixed by estimating vol on the gate-independent stream with an expanding-window fallback. A sizing bug fix, not a parameter search; run 1 is reported so the change is auditable.

verdict_rule: promising: OOS Sharpe >= 0.8 and DSR >= 0.9 and null p <= 0.05; marginal: OOS Sharpe > 0.3 and CAGR > 0 and null p <= 0.2; else fails
caveats: HEADLINE FAILS: stitched walk-forward OOS 2022-01..2025-06 (long-only, 144 configs, rolling 730/182): CAGR -15.9%, Sharpe -0.86, MaxDD -52.9%; 2022 -6.8%, 2023 -41.5%, 2024 +8.4%, 2025H1 -7.7%. Deflated Sharpe ~0.

Costs are the killer: the same OOS entries with zero fees/slippage/funding give Sharpe 0.47 / CAGR 7.3%. Net, fee+slippage drag is 23%/yr of equity at ~214x turnover. Stop-market entries and stops are taker fills by construction, so there is no maker-rebate escape.

Random-day null (same symbols/sides/sizes/stop distances, random session opens, 200 draws): strategy at the 85th percentile, p=0.15. Timing beats random days, but not significantly; random days themselves average Sharpe -1.3 after costs.

FROZEN (1d, k=0.8, prior H-L, MA10, no BTC gate) was picked for half-year stability over 2020H2-2025H1. Its dev Sharpe 0.68 / CAGR 13% / DD -41% comes from 2020-21 (+50%, +43%). With those params fixed, 2022-2025H1 Sharpe is -0.01 (2022 -31%), even though the params were chosen with hindsight. k=0.8 sits on the grid edge: dev Sharpe rises with k because fewer trades means lower costs. The WF never chose it.

Walk-forward selection is unstable: 7 folds chose 7 different configs. Fold 2023H2 picked a 6h config on a train Sharpe of 0.03 and lost 36%. POST-HOC diagnostics (not the verdict basis): a 1d-only WF gives OOS Sharpe -0.21 (CAGR -5.1%); a BTC+ETH-only 1d WF gives -0.34 (CAGR -9.1%). Every variant is negative OOS.
6h sessions (4 order cycles/day) are ruinous after costs: median dev Sharpe -2.5, and every 6h config has a negative dev Sharpe. More trades per day makes this family worse, not better.
L/S variant (separate 144-config WF; shorts only when coin < MA and BTC < 200d MA): OOS Sharpe 0.04, CAGR -1.5%, MaxDD -46%. Shorts helped in 2025H1 (+26%) but lost in 2023 (-26%).

Phase-1 evidence reproduces in-sample only: BTC/ETH k=0.7 MA20 at 1% risk gives dev Sharpe 0.83 and DD -8%, but only 7.5% CAGR at ~0.04x average exposure. Walk-forward on BTC/ETH is negative (see above).

$200 implementability: 12.4% of OOS entries fall below Bybit minimums (BTC minOrderQty 0.001 accounts for about half, then ETH and SOL). With rounding, OOS Sharpe is -0.80. There are no symbol-name mismatches.

Modelling: run_events has no conditional ENTRY order, so the module splits each trigger hour (see harness). Trigger + stop in the same 1h bar is always counted as a loss (pessimistic). The extra 3bp slippage is applied to every fill, time exits included (slightly pessimistic). Two timing effects are not modelled: live orders go in at 00:07 rather than 00:00, and the time exit happens at 00:07 rather than at the 00:00 open. Funding is charged: 1.3%/yr in the OOS.

Universe: the first 12 of data.MAJORS, a list of long-lived survivors, with a PIT top-20 liquidity mask. The column choice is survivorship-biased, which is optimistic, so a truly point-in-time top-10 universe would likely do worse.

Sizing bug fixed between runs. Run 1 estimated vol from the gated stream, so the scale blew up to its 5x clip after a no-trade gated fold. Run 1's OOS Sharpe was -0.11. The gap to run 2's -0.86 comes almost entirely from different fold choices (the 2023H2 pick), which shows how fragile the selection is. Both runs fail.
The OOS return distribution has a fat right tail (skew 2.6, kurtosis 26), so a handful of breakout days carry the P&L and the win rate is 40%. Payoff is 1.25, too small for that win rate after costs.
lab_issues_found: sim.run_events cannot model a conditional (stop-market) ENTRY or a resting limit ENTRY: entries always fill at the next bar's open. The task text says such resting orders are 'modelled in run_events' -- only exits (stop/target/trail/time) are. Worked around in strategies/vol_breakout.py by a split-bar sim panel; the lab itself is unchanged.

wf.walk_forward(kind='events') runs the entries on the same panel the strategy received, so a strategy that needs a derived sim panel (as above) cannot use it; re-implemented here with wf.make_folds and identical selection/stitching semantics.
